keyFindings.description: The renewal rule is `if renewal_window > lifetime.value`, so 3 x heartbeat + call_budget == lifetime passes. The rule's own failure text says the third refresh 'does not complete inside the lifetime... still owes its round trip - and setInterval fires late', which is exactly as true at equality as one millisecond past it, and the success path then prints that the window is 'inside' the lifetime. This is the half of the architect's round-1 ruling that is not in the code: it asked for three attempts plus their call budget to fit STRICTLY inside, and the implementation delivered the slack (the + call_budget term) but kept a non-strict comparison. The PR body's Change list repeats the claim, 'strictly, so a boundary that the third refresh cannot complete inside no longer passes', which the comparison does not deliver. Reachable configuration: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS 14_875 with today's other constants gives a call budget of 30000 ms and a renewal window of exactly 300000 ms, and the check exits 0. Today's tree has 19750 ms of slack, so nothing lapses now; the defect is in the guard this change exists to leave behind. Fix: reject equality (>=), move the suggested maximum and minimum with it, and add a case at 3H + B == TTL - the suite's existing boundary case at check-heartbeat-margin.test.sh:143-157 is 3H == TTL, which the call budget already pushes past the lifetime, so it does not cover this one.

The two-interval rule (worst_case = 2 * heartbeat + call_budget) can never fail without the renewal rule failing first: 2H + B <= 3H + B for every heartbeat the parser accepts, so any tree that trips it has already tripped rule 1. It adds no rejection, only a second diagnostic for one violated margin with a different prescribed remedy - the suite's own worst-case fixture reports two problems prescribing minimum lifetimes of 300400 ms and 260400 ms, so following the weaker one leaves the stronger failing. Delete the branch and its duplicate assertions, and keep the backstop explanation in the header, which is the part that earns its place: it is the reason the pass deadline is not in the formula at all. This was my round-1 finding, and rule 1 gaining the call budget in round 3 subsumed it.

fenceAudit.result: No omitted fence re-read remains. The two deliberate exceptions are bounded: registerSession's clock stamp carries the session id it captured, so an old session's late reply cannot suppress the new one and the worst case is one extra registration outside the queues; settleEndedHolds' failed-hand-back restore can reintroduce bookkeeping a newer claim cleared, whose worst case is a redundant soft claim of a role the session already holds, or a hand-back to a listener that no longer names that session. Neither reaches the harm class the three fixed sites did. The architect routed the restore site to dispatch://INFRA-49/ask/c7051816-2e86-4cb6-ad56-02ccb01e9355 with its trace.
